lockup.summary: The company, its directors, executive officers and holders of nearly all its shares agreed not to sell for 180 days after the prospectus date. The lead underwriters can give written consent to sell earlier.

what: A clinical-stage drug company developing pain medicines that are not opioids and are meant to block pain signals without risk of addiction.
proceeds: The company expects net proceeds of about $315.7 million. About $124.7 million is for its lead drug LTG-001, through late-stage trials and an FDA application, and for getting ready to sell it. About $46.2 million is for LTG-321 trials. The rest is for other research, working capital and general costs.
risks: Latigo is a young company with a short history and has never sold a product, so its future is hard to judge.
It has lost a lot of money since it began and expects larger losses, and it may never make a profit.
Even with this offering, it will need much more money, which could dilute shareholders or force it to cut or stop its programs.
